answer: Keep your car insured until the sale is complete and the car is in our hands, then cancel or remove it from your policy only after you sign the paperwork, and ask your insurer about a refund for unused premium. What happens to your plates depends on the state that issued them: North Carolina plates stay on the car, but if your car has plates from another state, such as California, different rules apply (California plates must be returned within 10 days with form NW-PLT-1). Before handing over the car, remove toll tags and parking stickers, clear garage door codes, unpair your phone, and remove the car from any connected-car app account. If your car is registered in another state, it will also need an emissions certificate from a North Carolina inspection station before we can buy it at a North Carolina store.
